findings.title: Device is cached as tagged before the DB write, so a limit-rejected device is admitted on its retry
findings.body: tagDeviceUI sets the local cache key (line 87) before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice (line 93). When the limit is reached, CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, TagDevice returns that error, and Authenticate rejects the login. The cache entry is not removed, so it stays for 29 minutes. The next request from the same device ID hits the cache check at lines 83-85, tagDeviceUI returns nil, and the anonymous login succeeds without the device ever being stored or counted. The same happens after any transient DB error. The cache entry should be set only after a successful write, or deleted when the write fails.

findings.title: Requests without the device ID header are never counted or limited
findings.body: TagDevice returns nil when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent (lines 120-122). Authenticate only fails on ErrDeviceLimitReached, so an anonymous request that omits the header is neither stored nor rejected, and the limit does not apply to it. The header is client-supplied, so clients can also rotate IDs to get fresh slots. Before this change, tagging was only analytics and this gap did not matter. Now the feature is meant to enforce a limit, so the missing-header case should either be rejected while the limit is active or be documented as outside the limit.

findings.title: Count-then-insert is not atomic, so concurrent new devices can exceed the limit
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts devices (line 110) and compares with the limit (line 115), then runs the upsert (lines 120-155) with no transaction or lock. Many concurrent logins from new devices can all read a count below the limit and all insert, so the number of stored devices can exceed deviceLimit by up to the concurrency level. The check-and-insert needs to be atomic, for example in one transaction with a conditional insert, or the overshoot must be documented as acceptable.

findings.title: Device tagging moved from a background goroutine onto the synchronous auth path
findings.body: Previously TagDevice ran in a goroutine with a 2-minute timeout, off the request path. Now Authenticate calls it synchronously with the request context and no timeout. Each first request per device per instance performs a DB write during login, and when a limit is configured each new device also runs a COUNT over the updated_at range (database.go line 110). Slow DB calls now delay or block anonymous page loads, and the panic recovery from the goroutine is gone. The limit-enforcement design needs the synchronous write, but the cost on the hot path, including the uncached COUNT, should be assessed.

findings.title: No tests cover the Authenticate path, the cache interaction, or updates to existing devices at the limit
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for a new device. Nothing tests that a rejected device retried within the cache window is still rejected, which would have caught the cache bypass in impl.go. Nothing tests that Authenticate returns the error to the caller, or that an existing device still gets its updated_at refreshed (the updateDevice path) once the count has reached the limit. The new enforcement behaviour is therefore only covered at the store level.

findings.title: New auth.anonymous device_limit option is not documented
findings.body: The device_limit key is read here, but the PR changes no configuration documentation such as conf/defaults.ini or the docs for the [auth.anonymous] section, so operators have no way to learn that the key exists, that 0 means unlimited, or how the 30-day window counts devices. The PR description is also still the unfilled template, including the docs and feature-toggle checklist items.

findings.title: Dependency injection signature changed; wire files are not part of this diff
findings.body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now takes db.DB and builds the store itself, and anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore now requires an int64 that no provider in the graph supplies. If the wire provider set (wire.go or wire_gen.go) still binds anonstore.AnonStore or lists ProvideAnonDBStore, wire generation or compilation will fail. Those files are not in the changed list, so this should be checked.
